status: Closed — source repair, frozen runner publication, and TASK-MAO-0060 closeout verified 2026-09-05
finding: Framework batch checkpoint can deadlock when uncommitted source changes make the frozen runner stale: `node atm.mjs batch checkpoint` refuses with `ATM_RUNNER_STALE_WRITE_REFUSED`, the prescribed build can cache-hit or require publication against the previous HEAD, and `node atm.dev.mjs batch checkpoint` can perform partial close mutations before refusing lifecycle writes with `ATM_SOURCE_FIRST_WRITE_REFUSED`.
expectedBehavior: Batch checkpoint should provide one normal recovery path that either reserves/builds/publishes the frozen runner for the candidate staged source tree before close, or creates a governed commit-candidate/checkpoint bridge without requiring native Git emergency commits. Source-first lifecycle attempts must be dry-run or atomic when writes are forbidden.
evidenceOrRepro: ATM-GOV-0246 on 2026-07-29: `node atm.mjs batch checkpoint --actor codex-git-series-captain --json` returned `ATM_RUNNER_STALE_WRITE_REFUSED`; `npm run build` initially used sealed source `4ca233f09...`; `node atm.dev.mjs batch checkpoint` later wrote ATM-GOV-0246 close packet/events before returning `ATM_SOURCE_FIRST_WRITE_REFUSED`, forcing emergency bridge commits `1e4db7cfb` and `06618257d`. On 2026-09-02, `taskflow-source-first-close-no-write.test.ts` reproduced the pre-fix boundary failure (the source-first close reached `ATM_TASK_CLOSE_ACTIVE_CLAIM_REQUIRED`, not the source-first denial). The repair calls `assertSourceFirstRunnerReadOnlyAction` before the stale-runner and close transaction path; the same real CLI invocation now returns `ATM_SOURCE_FIRST_WRITE_REFUSED` and proves byte-identical task ledger plus no event, closure packet, or close journal.
followUp: The source-first side-effect defect and the frozen-runner checkpoint recovery bridge are both repaired. TASK-MAO-0060 delivered the candidate-bound recovery contract, source validation, sealed runner publication, and governed closeout.
